topic: North Magnetic Pole deviation >18° from 120°E longitude
change_summary: Priority-5 spot-check: WIN-036 had the oldest most-recent review in the corpus (c5 @ 2026-05-07, >3 months stale) per the dispatcher fall-through to Priority 5. Re-reviewed with fresh eyes to verify the two substantive c5 holes were closed and to re-attack the current text.
our_argument_summary: Verdict 'Std Model Explains' holds (data/wins.json:WIN-036.verdict). WIN-036 registers a binary threshold (>18° east of 120°E) that the dome confirms by transcribing WMM2025's published pole position 139.298°E and computing 139.298−120=19.298° (raw-text/02-wins.txt:124, raw-text/03-predictions.txt:67). Our review argues this is (i) post-hoc (WMM2025 released Dec 2024, PROS-006 registered 2026-03-06, ~14.6-month gap), (ii) non-discriminating (both the dome trajectory and WMM2025 are constrained by the same NOAA NP trajectory record and no divergent future-epoch prediction has been demonstrated), and (iii) a trivial arithmetic restatement of WIN-007's 139.3°E pole position (data/wins.json:WIN-036.detail_evidence). The dome's own source text corroborates (iii): raw-text/02-wins.txt:22 writes the confirmation as '-> WIN-007 + W010 (WIN-036)', chaining WIN-036 directly off WIN-007. c6 confirms both c5 holes are resolved.

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c5 hole #3 (minor), still unresolved as of git HEAD b533051: the detail_evidence sentence 'Both NOAA's WMM2025 secular-variation forecast and the dome's purported exponential trajectory are constrained by the same NOAA-authored North Magnetic Pole trajectory record...' uses the term 'secular-variation forecast' without a parenthetical gloss. holes_found.description: Traceability gap on a parenthetical date. detail_evidence states PROS-006 was 'registered on 6 March 2026 (confirmed 12 March 2026...)'. The registration date 2026-03-06 is directly sourced (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:40 'Registered 2026-03-06'), but the 'confirmed 12 March 2026' claim is not present in the raw-text I can read this run (raw-text/02-wins.txt / 03-predictions.txt carry only the registration date and the confirmed value, not a confirmation date). The confirmation date presumably lives in the live status_history.json, which was not fetched this run. Non-load-bearing (the post-hoc argument depends on the Dec-2024-vs-March-2026 gap, which the registration date alone establishes), but the parenthetical asserts a specific date our own repo text does not corroborate.
holes_found.recommendation: Either drop the '(confirmed 12 March 2026...)' parenthetical or add a snapshot citation to a captured status_history.json in data/dome-api-snapshots/ that carries the 2026-03-12 confirmation entry. Cheapest fix is to drop it — the registration date is the load-bearing one for the post-hoc test.

stronger_arguments.description: Lean harder on the dome's own WIN-007 chaining. The dome source (raw-text/02-wins.txt:22) writes the WIN-036 confirmation as '-> WIN-007 + W010 (WIN-036)', i.e. the author himself derives W010 as a corollary of the WIN-007 pole position rather than as an independent measurement. Our 'two phrasings of the same NOAA measurement' line could cite this directly: the double-count is not our inference, it is visible in the dome's own confirmation-mapping text. That converts 'we assert this is redundant with WIN-007' into 'the dome's own bookkeeping treats WIN-036 as an arithmetic consequence of WIN-007'.

Name a concrete divergence test (carried from c5 stronger_arguments #2, still not adopted). WMM2025's 5-year epoch publishes year-by-year pole positions through 2030. A genuinely independent dome prediction would commit — via a properly-anchored OTS scheme on a predictions-only document (see Timestamp Error tab) — a divergent pole position for epoch 2030.0 before the WMM2030 update publishes in late 2029. Naming this converts 'they have not been shown to make distinguishable predictions at any future epoch' from a passive observation into an actionable, dated challenge the dome can accept or visibly decline.
sources: Timestamp Error tab (the proper-anchoring scheme required)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author did build a quantitative, binary-threshold prediction (>18° east of 120°E) and registered it with a specific pass condition (data/wins.json:WIN-036.detail_claim; raw-text/03-predictions.txt:39-41). That is structurally the correct shape for a scientific prediction — a pre-stated threshold with an unambiguous pass/fail, rather than a vague post-hoc gesture. The pole genuinely IS at ~139°E and genuinely does exceed 18° from 120°E (arithmetic verified this run: 139.298−120=19.298°).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Correct shape does not confer prospective status. WMM2025 published 139.298°E in Dec 2024, ~14.6 months before PROS-006 was registered (2026-03-06), so the threshold was already known-exceeded at write-time (data/wins.json:WIN-036.detail_verdict_text; raw-text/03-predictions.txt:40-41). And the dome adds no discriminating mechanism: both its trajectory and WMM2025 are constrained by the same NOAA NP trajectory record, with no demonstrated divergent future-epoch prediction (data/wins.json:WIN-036.detail_evidence). Finally the dome's own confirmation text chains W010 off WIN-007 (raw-text/02-wins.txt:22), so it is an arithmetic restatement of an already-post-hoc pole position, not an independent confirmation. Verdict 'Std Model Explains' holds.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A dome defender who accepts our methodology principles could argue: 'A threshold-crossing prediction is a legitimate prediction form — like predicting a stock crosses $100. The fact that >18°-from-120°E is arithmetically entailed by a 139°E pole does not make it non-predictive; it makes it a testable corollary. And WIN-007 vs WIN-036 being linked in our bookkeeping is just internal traceability, not an admission of double-counting.' This is the strongest line, but it does not touch the post-hoc defect: the threshold was crossed and published (WMM2025, Dec 2024) more than a year before registration, so it is a corollary of a KNOWN value, and a corollary of a post-hoc value is still post-hoc. Our text already forecloses it ('two phrasings of the same NOAA measurement, not independent predictions').
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: No text change required to hold the verdict, but adopting stronger_arguments #1 (cite the dome's own '-> WIN-007 + W010' mapping) would drop this from 2 to 1 by making the double-count the dome's own admission rather than our inference.
advocate_mode.what_we_should_say_instead: Optionally append to the redundancy sentence: '— a dependency the dome's own confirmation log records directly, mapping W010's pass to WIN-007's pole position.'
